note: Shows one progression worked several ways: heard as arpeggios with only the roots played, the shapes, strummed with a strum-along, then improvised over with each chord's 3rd lit. Same four chords, four different tools and tasks.

exercise.title: I-V-vi-IV in G, four ways
exercise.focus: G-D-Em-C · roots by ear · shapes · strumming at 80 · 3rds over each chord
exercise.why: I-V-vi-IV is under more pop songs than any other four chords, so it pays to know it from every side.

sections.text: Press Play to hear the progression as arpeggios. Play only each chord's root on the low strings, one note per bar: G, D, E, C. Switch the backing to hear it another way.
Press each chord box to hear it. Play the four shapes in order, at your own pace.
Press Play. The lit block is the chord to strum, one bar each. Start with one strum per beat. Then try the pattern down, down-up, up-down-up.
Press Play. Improvise in G major near the open chords. Land on each chord's 3rd when that chord comes round: {{b}} over G, {{f-sharp}} over D, {{g}} over Em, {{e}} over C.
